title: Ingress header rewrite during node drain causes API key misbinding to wrong org in Dedicated/Private
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Several Dedicated and Private customers reported intermittent cross-organisation access after node drains or autoscaling events. Root cause was a header rewrite at the dedicated ingress layer combined with transient API key resolution during refresh which allowed an in-flight request to be evaluated against the wrong tenant mapping. This ticket tracks the urgent investigation, customer mitigation, and the production fix rollout.

Affected surface: Dedicated GPU pools behind our HA ingress and Private (on-prem) installations that use the same ingress rewrite logic. Symptoms observed: a) Customer users in tenant A intermittently saw data or responses belonging to tenant B; b) Audit logs showed request-level apikey -> org bindings flipping during single session; c) Incidents mainly occurred during node drains, autoscale down, or restart of the dedicated gateway pods.

Timeline:
- 2026-02-26 03:14 UTC: Pager alert triggered by AcmeHealth (dedicated) active customer escalations.
- 2026-02-26 04:00 UTC: Initial triage, we reproduced with traffic replay in staging.
- 2026-02-26 09:00 UTC: Mitigation: increased ingress affinity and disabled header rewrite on suspect route for affected customers.

Reproduction steps (staging):
1) Deploy two gateway pods with identical config.
2) Send concurrent requests with API key X bound to org A.
3) Trigger node drain on pod1 while requests are mid-flight.
4) Observe that when ingress rewrites X-Org header during connection handover, subsequent identity lookup used a stale namespace cache and returned org B mapping for some requests.

Root cause analysis:
- In-flight request handover path updated header X-Org (internal traffic) as part of our dedicated ingress optimization.
- The API key resolver uses a two-level cache: a fast in-memory prefix cache + authoritative store refresh. During drain, a race allowed the handover to query the prefix cache while a background rotation/refresh was updating the authoritative mapping. The prefix cache returned a transiently stale mapping which had been re-bound in the authoritative store during a prior rotation window (edge case with overlapping key rebinds for certain tenants).
- The header rewrite mutated the internal header used for org-scoping before the final auth check returned; combined with a lack of atomic read/refresh semantics the request ended up authorized against the wrong org.

Immediate mitigation enacted:
- Disabled ingress header rewrite for dedicated/private gateway routes (hotfix) for all impacted customers (rolled out 2026-02-26 09:12 UTC).
- Increased prefix cache TTL to reduce cache churn during rotations.
- Added temporary strict affinity for dedicated pool placement to reduce drains during peak windows.

Fix description:
1) Make API key resolution read-after-refresh atomic: the resolver will now treat a cache miss as a single-flight fetch that blocks handover until authoritative mapping is confirmed (fix PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1248).
2) Stop mutable header rewrites during in-flight connection handover. Header rewrites must be idempotent and use the resolved org from the same resolver call (fix PR: github.com/redwood/edge/pull/612).
3) Add deterministic rotation fencing: when a key rotation occurs, the authoritative store increments a rotation epoch. Resolvers compare epoch to ensure they never return pre-rotation mappings after a rotation has been observed.

Testing & validation:
- Unit + integration tests for resolver single-flight behavior added.
- Chaos tests in staging to simulate node drains and concurrent rotations.
- Synthetic traffic replay against a staging cluster with identical scaling behaviour for 48h.
- Regression test asserting that request audit logs never show a change in apikey->org mapping mid-request.

Rollout plan:
- Stage rollout to non-customer staging clusters (complete).
- Canary to 3 low-impact dedicated customers for 2 days with heavy drain-simulated traffic (starting 2026-03-05).
- Gradual rollout across Dedicated pools, then Private packages (on-prem) via patch bundle (target completion: 2026-03-15).
- Monitor: per-request audit logs, org-mapping-flip metric, and SLO errors with 5m and 1h alert windows.

Monitoring queries and dashboards:
- org_mapping_flip_rate = sum(rate(auth.mapper.flip[5m])) by (pool)
- audit_discrepancies = count_over_time({env=\"prod\",event=\"auth_audit\",diff=true}[1h])
- Added temporary Grafana panel in \"Dedicated Reliability\" dashboard.

Customer communication:
- Notified impacted customers (AcmeHealth, BlueFin Analytics, MedData Corp) with RCA summary and mitigation steps.
- Provided temporary config to opt-out of ingress rewrites and offered account migration to a dedicated non-shared pool.

Open action items / follow-ups:
- (Postmortem) Complete customer-facing root cause write-up and publish with redacted logs (owner: PM: Priya Kumar).
- (Infra) Replace prefix cache with LRU+single-flight implementation and benchmark memory overhead (owner: Jonas Meyer).
- (Security) Full audit of rotation fencing semantics across Dedicated and Private (owner: Security team).
- Update runbook for \"auth namespace flip\" incidents (owner: oncall).

Notes on differences from prior apikey incidents: previous tickets focused on refresh races where revoked keys were briefly accepted; this issue is unique because header mutation plus cache single-flight missing atomicity produced cross-tenant data exposure during in-flight handover.
